v.en: O God, come to my assistance;

r.la: Et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.
r.en: And my mouth shall declare thy praise.

full.la: Prope est iam Dóminus, * Veníte, adorémus.
full.en: The Lord is now near * O come, let us adore Him.

short.en: O come, let us adore Him.

la: Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.

Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
en: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

v.en: From Sion, from the place of his greatness.

text.la: In Deo salutáre meum * et glória mea: et spes mea in Deo est.
text.en: In God is my salvation * and my glory: and my hope is in God.

text.la: Vidéte ópera Dómini, * et audítam fácite vocem laudis eius.
text.en: Behold the works of the Lord * and make the voice of his praise to be heard.

text.la: Audíte, omnes * qui timétis Deum, quanta fecit ánimæ meæ.
text.en: Come and hear, all ye that fear God * what great things he hath done for my soul.

text.la: Exsúrgat Deus, * et dissipéntur inimíci eius. ‡
text.en: Let God arise, * and let his enemies be scattered. ‡

text.la: Deus noster, * Deus salvos faciéndi: et Dómini sunt éxitus mortis.
text.en: Our God * is the God of salvation: and the Lord of the issues from death.
In the churches * bless ye God the Lord.

text.la: Salvum me fac, * Deus, quóniam intravérunt aquæ usque ad ánimam meam. ‡
text.en: Save me, O God * for the waters are come in even unto my soul. ‡

text.la: Propter inimícos meos * éripe me, Dómine.
text.en: O Lord, save me * from my enemies.

text.la: Quǽrite Dóminum, * et vivet ánima vestra.
text.en: Look for the Lord * and your soul shall live.

text.la: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
text.en: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

text.la: Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
text.en: O Lord Jesus Christ, graciously hear the prayers of Thy servants, and have mercy upon us, Who livest and reignest with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, ever world without end.

benedictio.la: Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.
benedictio.en: May the Eternal Father bless us with an eternal blessing.

source.en: Lesson from the book of Isaias

text.la: 1 Utinam dirúmperes cælos, et descénderes: a fácie tua montes deflúerent. 2 Sicut exústio ignis tabéscerent, aquæ ardérent igni, ut notum fíeret nomen tuum inimícis tuis: a fácie tua gentes turbaréntur. 3 Cum féceris mirabília, non sustinébimus: descendísti, et a fácie tua montes defluxérunt. 4 A sǽculo non audiérunt, neque áuribus percepérunt: óculus non vidit, Deus absque te, quæ præparásti exspectántibus te.
text.en: 1 That thou wouldst rend the heavens, and wouldst come down: the mountains would melt away at thy presence. 2 They would melt as at the burning of fire, the waters would burn with fire, that thy name might be made known to thy enemies: that the nations might tremble at thy presence. 3 When thou shalt do wonderful things, we shall not bear them: thou didst come down, and at thy presence the mountains melted away. 4 From the beginning of the world they have not heard, nor perceived with the ears: the eye hath not seen, O God, besides thee, what things thou hast prepared for them that wait for thee.

body.la: Cánite tuba in Sion, vocáte gentes, annuntiáte pópulis, et dícite:
body.en: Blow ye the trumpet in Zion, call together the nations, tell it out among the people, and say:

verse.la: Annuntiáte, et audítum fácite: loquímini, et clamáte.
verse.en: Tell it out and make it to be heard; speak aloud and cry.

benedictio.la: Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.
benedictio.en: May the Son, the Sole-begotten, mercifully bless and keep us.

text.la: 5 Occurrísti lætánti, et faciénti iustítiam: in viis tuis recordabúntur tui: ecce tu irátus es, et peccávimus: in ipsis fúimus semper, et salvábimur. 6 Et facti sumus ut immúndus omnes nos, et quasi pannus menstruátæ univérsæ iustítiæ nostræ: et cecídimus quasi fólium univérsi, et iniquitátes nostræ quasi ventus abstulérunt nos. 7 Non est qui ínvocet nomen tuum: qui consúrgat, et téneat te: abscondísti fáciem tuam a nobis, et allisísti nos in manu iniquitátis nostræ.
text.en: 5 Thou hast met him that rejoiceth, and doth justice: in thy ways they shall remember thee: behold thou art angry, and we have sinned: in them we have been always, and we shall be saved. 6 And we are all become as one unclean, and all our justices as the rag of a menstruous woman: and we have all fallen as a leaf, and our iniquities, like the wind, have taken us away. 7 There is none that calleth upon thy name: that riseth up, and taketh hold of thee: thou hast hid thy face from us, and hast crushed us in the hand of our iniquity.

body.la: Non auferétur sceptrum de Iuda, et dux de fémore eius, donec véniat qui mitténdus est:
body.en: The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, nor the law-giver from his loins, until he that shall be sent cometh.

refrain.en: And unto him shall the longing of the Gentiles be.

verse.la: Pulchrióres sunt óculi eius vino, et dentes eius lacte candidióres.
verse.en: His eyes shall be bright with wine, and his teeth white with milk.

benedictio.la: Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.
benedictio.en: May the grace of the Holy Spirit enlighten all our hearts and minds.

text.la: 8 Et nunc, Dómine, pater noster es tu, nos vero lutum: et fictor noster tu, et ópera mánuum tuárum omnes nos. 9 Ne irascáris, Dómine, satis, et ne ultra memíneris iniquitátis nostræ: ecce réspice, pópulus tuus omnes nos. 10 Cívitas sancti tui facta est desérta, Sion desérta facta est, Ierúsalem desoláta est. 11 Domus sanctificatiónis nostræ, et glóriæ nostræ, ubi laudavérunt te patres nostri, facta est in exustiónem ignis, et ómnia desiderabília nostra versa sunt in ruínas.
text.en: 8 And now, O Lord, thou art our father, and we are clay: and thou art our maker, and we all are the works of thy hands. 9 Be not very angry, O Lord, and remember no longer our iniquity: behold, see we are all thy people. 10 The city of thy sanctuary is become a desert, Sion is made a desert, Jerusalem is desolate. 11 The house of our holiness, and of our glory, where our fathers praised thee, is burnt with fire, and all our lovely things are turned into ruins.

body.la: Me opórtet mínui, illum autem créscere: qui autem post me venit, ante me factus est:
body.en: I must decrease, but He must increase; He it is Who, coming after me is preferred before me;

refrain.la: Cuius non sum dignus corrígiam calceamentórum sólvere.
refrain.en: Whose shoe's latchet I am not worthy to unloose.

verse.la: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
verse.en: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

text.la: Reliqua omittuntur, nisi Laudes separandæ sint.
text.en: Skip the rest, unless praying Lauds separately.

text.la: Excita, quǽsumus, Dómine, poténtiam tuam, et veni: et magna nobis virtúte succúrre; ut per auxílium grátiæ tuæ, quod nostra peccáta præpédiunt, indulgéntia tuæ propitiatiónis accéleret:
text.en: Stir up, we beseech thee, O Lord, thy power, and come; make haste to our aid with thy great might; that, by the help of thy grace, that which is hindered by our sins may be hastened by thy merciful forgiveness.

office.title: Feria V infra Hebd IV Adventus
